title: Part-mesh alias table: topology `part` id -> mesh provenance `part_id`
notes: A topology edge's `part` (docs/DAG_TOPOLOGY.md's vocabulary, authored per-edge) and an installed mesh's provenance.json `part_id` (the tessellation run's own naming, data/meshes/README.md) are two namespaces with zero exact matches at 2026-09-10. This table is the one sanctioned bridge between them (strategy brief BRIEF_20260909_topology_part_vocabulary_mesh_mapping, option b: declared configuration, never fuzzy matching, never renaming installed meshes).

Every entry asserts 'these two strings name the same physical part' and carries the evidence for that identity -- the mesh's own provenance.json, data/meshes/README.md, or a drawing number. A pair whose identity cannot be evidenced stays out of this table: the annotate app's 'no installed mesh' empty state is the honest answer, never a guessed match.
Values map to a mesh's `part_id`, not its sha256, so a re-tessellated mesh installed under the same part identity keeps its aliases.

The eleven `asm217755_*` rows were added by handoff extracted_mesh_alias_rows (2026-09-15) against the piece-part meshes rotorkit's assembly_step_part_extraction (2026-09-14) extracted from `217755-001 A.1 PROPULSION ASSEMBLY, PROPELLER, CW Released.stp` and installed into data/meshes/. Each row is an exact drawing- or spec-number match on both sides, with the mesh side read off the live provenance.json at merge time rather than transcribed. Five further topology part ids stayed OUT at that point, as candidates rather than rows, each needing a decision nothing in the STEP can settle; what each one needed is recorded in docs/sessions/lessons/LESSONS_20260915_extracted_mesh_alias_rows.md.

Three of those five candidates were decided by handoff vpa_pitch_linkage_topology_and_feature_fits (2026-09-30), on parts-list evidence that had not been read when they were filed, and became the six rows at the foot of this table. Candidate 1 (`tan_link_mount_215175_002`, the dash number): 217755-001 A.1's parts list carries BOTH dash numbers, find 41 `215175-001 ... CW` qty 1 and find 73 `215175-002 ... CCW` qty '-', so the CW assembly every mesh here came from contains the -001. Candidate 2 (two `spherical_bearing_*` ids against three MS141xx meshes): 213862-002 A's own parts list is `213861-002` x1 plus `MS14101-3` x2, and the `_9bfdb344` mesh's two instances both sit under `213862-002.1` -- so that one is the pitch link's, `_84a75703` (three instances, one per `212956-005`) is the tangential link's, and `MS14103-3` is the tangential link's other end. Candidate 4 (`gas_spring`): see its own row. Candidates 3 (the two `flanged_bushing_*` ids) and 5 (`asm217755_214723_002`, installed with no candidate id) are UNCHANGED and still out, and so is `spherical_bearing_in_vpa` -- which candidate 2's resolution leaves with no mesh at all, since all three MS141xx geometries are now accounted for in the two links and none of them is in the VPA.

Consumed by apps/annotate/commands.js `resolveMeshIdentifier` (exact match, consulted only after a direct sha256/part_id match misses) and, since handoff annotate_affordances_flyout_and_mesh_gating (2026-09-14), by scripts/build_topology_projection.py `resolve_mesh` -- the same precedence in Python, so the topology projection can stamp per-part mesh availability for the viewer to gate its 3D affordances on. Paired against both live vocabularies by tests/test_part_mesh_aliases.py and apps/annotate/run_tests.cjs's [real] tier.

Spec number plus instance path, which together pick ONE of the two MS14101-3 geometries in this store. The pitch link assembly 213862-002's own parts list (drawing-checker run 20260922_154236_213862-002-A, sheet 1) is exactly two rows: 213861-002 PITCH LINK, PROPELLER qty 1, and MS14101-3 qty 2. This mesh's provenance.json (data/meshes/9bfdb34447e87a747dc2ebd696ef42dcacc63d70cb3483726220a0a46ddffffb) records product_name 'MS14101-3' at XCAF label 0:1:1:249 with exactly TWO instances, 213862-002.1/MS14101-3.1 and .2 -- the right spec number, the right count, under the right assembly. docs/topologies/topology_pitch_link_to_pitch_plate.json's part is named 'pitch-link spherical bearing (unconfirmed)'; this row is what confirms it.

The OTHER MS14101-3 geometry, picked by the same instance-path evidence from the other side. This mesh (data/meshes/84a75703551679078278209fc46b2859fa1ed798412f1fcf6ddff4166d000cca, product_name 'MS14101-3_2', XCAF label 0:1:1:1436) has three instances, one inside each of prd-e-03438709.1/.2/.3 -- the three instances of 212956-005, which 217755-001 A.1's parts list calls out at qty 3 (find 25, PITCH ANTI ROTATION LINK ASSEMBLY). Three tangential links, three of these bearings. The two MS14101-3 directories are distinct SOLIDS under one spec number, which is why the store suffixes each with its geometry signature; fitting both reads the same ball radius and the same race-seat radius, as two copies of one catalog part should.

Exact spec number on both sides, with the same structural corroboration. docs/topologies/topology_vpa_pitch_linkage.json's part is the tangential link's wide-series bearing, MS14103-3; the mesh's provenance.json (data/meshes/8ec0c0cdb02c62b4daebad103d8d6c49f178f5777c63027229c195a6281c5d48) records product_name 'MS14103-3' at XCAF label 0:1:1:1435, three instances, one inside each prd-e-03438709 -- the same three tangential links. docs/spec_library's event 0006 (RBC Aerospace plain bearings, pp. 21-22) records MS14103-3 as the wide-series bearing with the same .1900 in bore as MS14101-3, and the fit agrees: this mesh's spherical faces read a larger radius than either MS14101-3's.

Exact drawing number on both sides. docs/topologies/topology_vpa_pitch_linkage.json's part carries drawing 212956-005; the mesh's provenance.json (data/meshes/0196e26b8aa240cfd1da1bb4b8fbe5276e42fc054a5120cc4db27adafbde2a8a) records product_name '212956-005' at XCAF label 0:1:1:1434, four solids, three instances -- matching 217755-001 A.1 find 25's qty 3. NOTE what this mesh is: the whole link ASSEMBLY, four solids -- the body, an MS14101-3, an MS14103-3 and a bolt -- not the bare link, which is installed separately as `asm217755_213863_004`.

The dash-number question the 2026-09-15 candidate list left open, answered by the assembly's own parts list rather than by a judgement: 217755-001 A.1 (drawing-checker run 20260909_174538, sheet 1) carries find 41 '215175-001 TANGENTIAL LINK MOUNT ASSEMBLY, PROPELLER, CW' qty 1 and find 73 '215175-002 TANGENTIAL LINK MOUNT ASEMBLY, PROPELLER, CCW' qty '-'. READ THIS BEFORE USING THE ROW: the two dash numbers are the two HANDS of one design, not two revisions of one part, so this alias does not claim they are the same solid. It claims that the tangential link mount of the assembly every mesh in this store came from -- the CW 217755-001 -- is the -001, and that it is the mount the -002 topology part describes, mirrored. A reader looking at this mesh for a CCW build is looking at the mirror image. The mesh is data/meshes/cb58bf131e41af1852026bca8b2b61dec61327050c5e6a5054f84ed8b761cff7, product_name '215175-001', 40 solids: the mount INSTALLATION, whose machined detail 215198-001 is installed separately as `asm217755_215198_001` and whose own height 79.00 +/-0.10 is traced to 215198-A sheet 1 (2026-09-10).

A named human source plus structural corroboration, which is what the 2026-09-15 candidate list asked for and did not have ('structural adjacency only' was the reason it stayed out). The named source: Jeff, 2026-09-30, founding the `linkage` solver repo, listing the pitch linkage's rigid bodies and naming 'gas spring PMF200521 (body + rod)' as the gas spring of the pitch plate + piston body -- recorded in docs/sessions/HANDOFF_20260930_vpa_pitch_linkage_topology_and_feature_fits.md. The corroboration: this mesh (data/meshes/46a012dd9e7624f43811cedf1c6ff4ecc0f9af6e7a8b3f1e81b4e2177130eaf8) is a two-solid vendor item -- body and rod, exactly as named -- occurring three times inside 215176-002, the sub-assembly that also holds 213668-002, the gas-spring MOUNT already aliased in this table. What is NOT evidence here, and is worth a reader's attention: 217755-001 A.1's parts list carries no gas-spring row at all. That release carries a HYDRAULIC BRAKE ASSEMBLY instead (217676-001, find 85), so the gas spring in this STEP is the earlier configuration -- which is the configuration the pitch linkage this alias serves is modelled in.
